literal_source_claim_en: A condition for the existence of a perfect matching.
source_attribution: William Tutte, 1947 (catalog metadata; primary article identity strongly supported but exact source mapping unreviewed)
canonical_statement: A finite graph has a perfect matching if and only if, for every set U of vertices, deleting U leaves at most |U| connected components of odd order.
canonical_claim: A finite graph has a perfect matching if and only if, for every set U of vertices, deleting U leaves at most |U| connected components of odd order.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: {V : Type u} -> {G : SimpleGraph V} -> [Finite V] -> ((Exists fun M : G.Subgraph => M.IsPerfectMatching) <-> (forall u : Set V, not (G.IsTutteViolator u)))

domain_and_universes: Frozen Lean-facing target: V : Type u in any universe, G : SimpleGraph V, and [Finite V], with no explicit Fintype, DecidableEq, adjacency-decidability, connectedness, nonemptiness, or even-cardinality binder. Primary-source fidelity and master acceptance remain open.
quantifiers: for every finite simple graph G
ordered_binders: U : Set V inside the right side of the equivalence
hypotheses: G is represented as a simple undirected loopless graph
conclusion: The existence of a spanning matching subgraph of G is equivalent to every deleted vertex set leaving no more odd connected components than its cardinality.
degenerate_case_status: No finite carrier is excluded.
